answer: Randomized Slot Auction.** Each round, a public verifiable random draw assigns identities to a limited set of work slots on a shared jetty ledger. Only drawn identities can submit that round; the seed is revealed after commitments, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will win. To occupy many slots, an attacker must control many identities across every delta of rounds, and each rejected identity still pays a small per-round registration quill fee. Sustained sybil presence therefore costs linearly in identities times rounds, with no guarantee of selection.
